meta.name: Notion DNA
meta.legal_note: Notion's brand guidelines prohibit copying its look and feel. Use this to learn the system and combine it with your own identity. This is not legal advice.
meta.evidence_limits: Notion explains blocks and bricks at length, but says almost nothing about color, type choice, hover hiding or motion. Those rules come from pixels or are inferred. No clear block handle, current slash menu or live published Site screen was found.

soul.one_line: A quiet white page of same-sized rows where the user's emoji, covers and colored tags are the only things with personality.
soul.lineage: Word processors and early Macintosh software, by way of the 1960s and 70s computing pioneers Notion names.
soul.read_distance: Reading distance at a desk: built for working in for hours, not for glancing at.
philosophy: Everything is one unit, a block. [first-party]
Add a reusable brick, not a fixed feature. [first-party]
Give beginners ready-made boxes that still come apart. [first-party]
Make the plain path great; distrust the clever. [first-party, reported]
Avoid bright colors in the app. [first-party, reason not given]

colors.name: warm off-white
colors.note: Coverage varies: 0 with the sidebar closed, about 25 with it open. It takes space from the page.

user_colors.rule: Color belongs to the user's content. Tags are pale fill with dark same-hue text.
user_colors.count: Third-party count: 10 per theme. Not first-party.

banned_behaviours: Saturated color as a surface in the app's own chrome.
More than one blue button on a view.
A brand color anywhere in the frame.

families.family: A plain humanist sans; system UI stack
families.note: Users can switch a page to Default, Serif or Mono. That choice of three is first-party.

scale.display_to_body_ratio: Page title about 2.6x body, measured by eye

treatment.measure: Centered page column, about 54% of window width with sidebar open

space.grid: One sidebar and one centered text column. Blocks stack; columns are opt-in.
space.alignment: Everything starts at one left edge. Icon, title and body share it.
space.rhythm: One row height repeats for sidebar rows, list rows, table rows and menu rows
space.negative_space: Generous above the title; tight between blocks
space.safe_area: The empty margin around the column is where controls appear

surface.edges: Radius about 4 to 6px on rows and callouts, small on tags. Never pill-heavy, except view tabs.
surface.elevation: Flat. Only floating menus get a shadow.
surface.imagery: User-chosen covers. Line-drawn black and white for anything the product supplies itself.
surface.iconography: Thin grey monochrome for chrome. Full-color emoji for content. The two never swap jobs.

signatures.how: Sidebar rows, list rows, table rows and menu items share a height and a [small icon][label] shape, and hover gets the same pale fill.
signatures.never: A new row style per feature

signatures.how: Optional cover about 28% of content height, emoji at 2.5x title cap height overlapping its bottom edge, then a title at 2.6x body. All on one left edge.
signatures.never: A header bar with a page name inside it

signatures.how: Chrome stays within warm greys. Emoji, covers and tags are the only saturated marks, always placed by the user.
signatures.never: Colored icons in the product's own chrome

signatures.how: Pale pastel fill with a same-hue dark label, small radius, height about 0.75x the row.
signatures.never: White text on a saturated pill

signatures.how: Soft grey fill, no border, emoji at left, the block's contents inside.
signatures.never: Bordered or shadowed cards in body content

signatures.how: Page and block controls stay out of sight, grey and icon-only; a label appears only on the one primary action and on Share. [behavior documented; the reason is inferred]
signatures.never: A permanent toolbar of labeled buttons over content

signatures.how: A thin top bar holds a small icon-and-name path at left and sparse grey icons at right, with no fill.
Most choices live in plain text menus. A link is grey underlined text, and + New page is a faint row at the list end.
signatures.never: A big colored Add button for each list

weird_move.name: A glossy emoji on a monochrome page
weird_move.what: A large, detailed, full-color emoji sits on an otherwise colorless interface, overlapping the cover's edge at about 2.5x title height.
weird_move.rule: It's the only rich image the page needs. It always belongs to the user, and it is the first thing they customize.

archetypes.anatomy: breadcrumb, optional cover, big emoji, title, stacked blocks
icon and title, view tabs left, grey tool icons and one blue New right, hairline grid, faint + New page row
columns headed by a pale tag; flat cards with hairline
workspace switcher, few utilities, grey section labels, nested rows with chevron and emoji
account row, horizontal cards with mini cover and emoji, inset grouped rows with chevron and plus
A ready-made arrangement of ordinary blocks the user can pull apart. [first-party idea; layout inferred]

motion.durations: Unknown: nothing first-party, and stills can't show it

voice.headline_shape: The user's own words: the page's name

bans: Never give the product's own frame a saturated color.
Never use pure black for text.
Never add a second row style when the existing row can hold it.
Never put a shadow or border on body-content boxes.
Never use more than one filled button per view.
Never show a toolbar of labeled buttons over content.
Never use emoji for chrome or line icons for user content.
Never use a pill for a content tag.
Never add a one-off feature when a reusable block would do it.
Never leave someone at a blank page without a starter box.

tests.check: Chrome colors have under 12 points between their highest and lowest RGB channel, excluding one primary button
At most 3 font sizes, excluding emoji
Largest to smallest type is at most 3.2:1, excluding emoji
No box-shadow except on floating menus
At most one filled primary button
Row-like elements share one height, within 2px
Tags have a radius of 6px or less and pale fills
Every emoji sits on content the user owns, none in chrome

gaps_found: Round 1: links were grey and underlined across emoji; they are ink with text-only underline
Round 1: too little air between emoji and title
Round 1: linked rows were too tight
Round 1: selected row was not emphasized
Round 1: emoji size contradicted the type tests
Round 1: Share label contradicted the no-label ban
round_2_gaps: Sidebar chevrons still missing: the rule needs to be plainer
Selected state landed on the wrong row
Callout padding had to shrink to fit the height
reconstruction.verdict: Round 2 matches structure, hierarchy and rhythm on one screen, the page with sidebar. A stranger could still tell: system font and emoji differ, and no illustration on the cover. Other archetypes, dark mode and motion were never rebuilt.

page_anatomy.emoji: Starts on the page column left edge and overlaps the cover bottom by about half. Emoji size is excluded from the type tests.
page_anatomy.gaps: About 55pt of air between emoji and title. 16pt from title to first block. 8pt between callouts.
page_anatomy.links: Link text stays primary ink color with a 1px grey underline under the text only, not the emoji. Inline emoji sits before the link, outside the underline. Linked rows inside a callout are 32pt apart.
page_anatomy.sidebar: Rows have a grey chevron at far left when they have children, then the emoji, then the label. Teamspace rows use a small grey tile icon and no chevron. Selected row: pale fill, primary ink, weight 500. 16pt gap above each teamspace group. Every page row with children must show its chevron.
page_anatomy.breadcrumb: First crumb has a small grey tile icon. Separator is a faint slash. Share stays a text label; it is the one labeled top-bar control.
page_anatomy.callout: Padding 16pt; emoji in a 40pt left column; radius 4.
